narrative.overview:
The site is a dark command deck that has already read the file and is telling you what matters. Steel headlines are set in condensed uppercase, the small print is mono, and the whole surface is square, hairline-ruled, and quiet — until something is actionable, at which point one signal orange appears and nothing else does. It is industrial and high-contrast without raising its voice: the palette is nearly black, the type carries the hierarchy, and every border is a single pixel.

Atmosphere is built from two moves and no more. Tonal surfaces step from ink-base through ink-3 so that a card, a callout, or a search field sits on the page rather than floating above it. And a hairline rule separates every region, doubling on hover. The page itself is flat ink — no texture, no pattern, nothing behind the type.

Motion is small and instrumental: 0.12–0.2s transitions on a single curve, buttons and cards shifting border color, cards lifting 2px on hover with corner ticks fading in. Nothing bounces, nothing glows, nothing scrolls itself.
keyCharacteristics: Dark ink base (#090a0b) with four deliberate surface steps and no shadows at all.
Square everywhere: radius 0, 1px hairlines, corner brackets, no pills.
Condensed uppercase display type against 15.5px body copy capped at 54em.
Mono for every caption, label, table head, and tab — the instrument layer.
One accent per page: signal orange (#ff4a1c), or 2042 teal (#2fe0c8) inside the 2042 docs, never both.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Accent appears on ≤10% of any viewport and only where the reader can act or is already standing: primary actions, the current item, the focused element, the matched search term. Its rarity is the whole point — a screen with two orange things has no signal.

rules.name: The Teal Means 2042 Rule
rules.body: Teal exists to mark Battlefield 2042 documentation and never appears as a second accent on a 2042 page. No page shows both orange and teal.

rules.name: The Steel Is Type Rule
rules.body: Cold steel is a typographic color, not a background or a border fill. Surfaces are ink; steel is what is written on them.

rules.name: The Two-Face Rule
rules.body: Uppercase belongs to Big Shoulders and mono labels. Body copy is never tracked, never uppercase, never condensed — Barlow at 15.5px/1.65 is the reading voice and it does not get a costume.

rules.name: The 54em Rule
rules.body: Prose never exceeds 54em (roughly 70 characters at this size); the hero body caps at 46em. Widening a text column is not a way to fill space — the third rail column exists for that.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Decree Rule
rules.body: No outer shadows, no glows, no blurs, no textures or patterns on the page. If an element needs to come forward, it changes surface color or border color, or it moves 2px. A shadow is a bug.

rules.name: The Seamless Header Rule
rules.body: The sticky header is the same ink as the page, with no rule under it and no translucent layer over it. It is the mark and the actions, not a strip across the top.

rules.name: The Dead Square Rule
rules.body: Radius 0. A new component that would look better rounded does not belong in this system; find the edge, the bracket, or the rule instead.

rules.name: The Bracket Rule
rules.body: Corner ticks mark the element under the cursor, and they are the only chrome that ever appears on hover besides a border and a background step. They do not animate on entry beyond a 0.16s opacity fade, and they never appear at rest.

dos: Do keep accent usage under 10% of the viewport and only on actionable or current-state elements (The One Signal Rule).
Do build depth from the ink ladder (base #090a0b → ink-1 #0f1113 → ink-2 #15181b → ink-3 #1c2024) and a 1px border that shifts to rule-strong (#363d44) on interaction.
Do set every caption, label, table head, tab name, and keycap in JetBrains Mono at 11px with 0.14em tracking.
Do keep prose at 54em max, 15.5px, 1.65 line-height, in quiet text (#a4aeb9) — the reading environment is the product.
Do use uppercase Big Shoulders for headings and square, bracket-marked containers for structure; both are load-bearing for the industrial read.
Do swap the whole accent to 2042 teal (#2fe0c8) via `[data-game="bf2042"]` when the page documents Battlefield 2042.
donts: Don't add shadows, glows, gradient text, or blurred glass anywhere (The Flat-By-Decree Rule).
Don't round a corner. No 2px, no 4px, no pills, no circles — a rounded element is a foreign object in this system (The Dead Square Rule).
Don't show signal orange and 2042 teal on the same page, or use teal for anything outside Battlefield 2042 documentation.

Don't drift gamer-neon (glow, neon gradients, esports chrome), SaaS-marketing (gradient meshes, rounded soft cards, illustration blobs, social proof bars), or editorial-warm (serif body, cream paper, oversized italic pull quotes). All three are confirmed anti-references.
Don't adopt Material defaults: no ripple, no elevation ladder, no 4/12px radii, no Roboto.
Don't tint a hint's background with its semantic color, or use amber/red for emphasis — they mean warning and error, nothing else.
Don't add a texture, dot grid, or pattern behind the page; the surface is flat ink.
